Yes, if it is on a floating rate: Kaveri Bank charges nothing to prepay or close a floating-rate home loan. Personal, two-wheeler and car loans have their own rules (see the prepayment and foreclosure rules)."},{"doc_id":"kb-prepayment-rules","title":"Kaveri Bank (fictional): prepayment and foreclosure rules for loans","date":"2026-11-01","section":"Personal loans: part-prepayment and foreclosure","passage":"Personal loans: part-prepayment and foreclosure
Part-prepayment is allowed once 6 EMIs have been paid: up to 25% of the principal outstanding, once in any 12 months, free of charge.

Foreclosure (closing the loan in full) is allowed once 6 EMIs have been paid. The foreclosure charge is a share of the principal outstanding on the day of closure:

| EMIs paid | Foreclosure charge |
| --- | --- |
| 6 to 12 | 4.50% of the principal outstanding |
| 13 to 24 | 3.25% of the principal outstanding |
| 25 or more | 2.00% of the principal outstanding |"},{"doc_id":"kb-loan-products","title":"Kaveri Bank (fictional): loan products and interest rates","date":"2026-11-01","section":"Personal loans for salaried customers","passage":"Personal loans for salaried customers
Kaveri Bank's personal loans have a fixed rate for the whole tenure, set by the CIBIL score at approval:

| CIBIL score | Rate (percent a year) |
| --- | --- |
| 780 and above | 11.85% |
| 740 to 779 | 12.60% |
| 700 to 739 | 14.25% |
| Below 700 | Not offered |

Loan amount ₹50,000 to ₹25 lakh; tenure 12 to 60 months. For the processing fee see the schedule of charges; for prepayment see the prepayment and foreclosure rules."}]}
